name: Slovenia
summary: Slovenia taxes capital gains and dividends at 25%. The capital gains rate falls to 20% after 5 years, 15% after 10 and 0% after 15 years of holding. Children are fully exempt from inheritance and gift tax, and there is no wealth tax. No special regime for wealthy arrivals.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Worldwide taxation of residents; capital income taxed separately at schedular rates as a final tax.
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident under the permanent residence, habitual abode, centre of vital interests or 183-day tests.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains on shares, bonds, fund units and real estate are taxed at a flat 25% final tax (Art. 132 ZDoh-2), reduced by holding period: 20% after 5 years, 15% after 10 years, and exempt after 15 years. Applies to domestic and foreign assets alike.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Exempt after 15 years of holding (20 years until 31 Dec 2021). Main home exempt if owned, registered as permanent residence and actually lived in for the last 3 years. Gains inside an individual investment account (INR, from 5 Mar 2026) are taxed only on withdrawal at 15%, and the first withdrawal after 15 years is exempt; contributions are capped (EUR 20,000 in year one, then EUR 5,000/yr plus EUR 5,000 for Slovenian instruments, EUR 150,000 lifetime), so INR is immaterial for a large portfolio.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Holding period counted per lot under FIFO (Art. 103 ZDoh-2). Losses offset only capital gains of the same year; a 30-day wash-sale rule disallows losses where identical securities are bought 30 days before or after.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: A gift of capital is a disposal for the donor, but for gifts to a spouse or child the gain can be deferred to the recipient's later sale (application within 15 days). Inheritance is not a disposal. Derivatives are taxed under a separate tax on gains from derivative instruments.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Rates shown assume holding beyond 15 years (0%). Shorter holdings: 25% (0–5 years), 20% (5–10), 15% (10–15). An actively rebalanced portfolio will realise most gains at 25%.
capital_gains.professional_trader: If securities trading is carried on as a business activity, the income becomes business income under the progressive scale (top bracket 45% or 50% depending on the year, per the FURS guide; not verified for 2026) instead of capital gains; private investing is normally treated as capital gains.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: 25% → 20% after 5 years → 15% after 10 years → 0% after 15 years; FIFO per identical security.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents are taxed on worldwide gains; foreign tax paid can be credited. Must self-report gains on foreign brokers (annual return by 28 Feb).
open_questions: No deemed-disposal exit tax for individuals is described in the FURS 2026 capital income guide; not checked against the full ZDoh-2 text.

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed at a flat 25% final tax (Art. 132 ZDoh-2), with no holding-period reduction. Foreign dividends are taxed at 25% with a credit for foreign withholding tax.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: EUR 1,000 annual exemption applies only to interest on bank deposits with Slovenian/EU banks, not to dividends. INR account dividends are taxed only on withdrawal (15%).

dividends.withholding_outbound: PwC: standard 15% WHT on dividends paid to non-residents (0% to qualifying EU parent companies; treaty rates 0–15%). Dividends to individuals are subject to the 25% schedular tax.
dividends.treaty_network: 59 treaties in force (PwC), including the US, all major EU states, UK and Switzerland.

wealth_tax.summary: Slovenia has no net wealth tax and no annual levy on financial assets.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipalities levy a building-land use charge (NUSZ) on real estate. No general national real property tax was found to be in force for 2026 (not verified).

inheritance.summary: Inheritance and gift tax (ZDDD) is levied on the recipient, but children, adopted children and their descendants, spouse and unmarried partner (first inheritance order) are fully exempt, for both inheritances and gifts.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: First-order exemption (Art. 9 ZDDD) also covers sons/daughters-in-law and stepchildren. Other heirs: movables-only transfers below EUR 5,000 exempt.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Rates for non-exempt recipients (Art. 8): 5%–14% (parents, siblings), 8%–17% (grandparents), 12%–39% (others). A lifetime gift of shares or real estate is a capital-gains disposal for the parent unless deferral to the child is claimed (see capital gains).

inheritance.gift_tax: Same tax as inheritance; gifts to children are exempt. Gifts must be declared within 15 days.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Applies to property received by Slovenian residents, including foreign assets; children exempt regardless.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Liability attaches to the recipient's residence or the location of Slovenian property; no tail rules found.
inheritance.spouse_note: Spouse and unmarried (extramarital) partner of the deceased are first-order heirs, fully exempt from inheritance and gift tax (ZDDD Art. 9; FURS).

regimes.name: Family holding company (d.o.o.)
regimes.description: The family holds the portfolio through a Slovenian d.o.o. owned by the parents. The company pays corporate income tax at 22% (2024-2028; 19% afterwards) on realised gains; a listed minority holding gets no gains exemption (the 50% exemption needs a stake of at least 8% and an employee). Dividends are excluded from the base except a flat 5% treated as non-deductible expense, so they bear 22% x 5% = 1.1%. Money taken out is taxed again as a dividend at 25%. Wealth tax (none) and inheritance tax (children exempt) are the same as for direct holding, so those metrics are inherited from the standard regime.
regimes.eligibility: Any Slovenian resident can found a d.o.o. Contributing an existing portfolio in kind is probably a disposal for the individual under ZDoh-2 (gain taxed at 25%, falling with the holding period to 0% after 15 years; not verified for contributions), so the structure is cheapest when funded with cash or with positions held over 15 years.
regimes.duration_note: A corporate structure under ordinary law with no time limit. The 22% rate is temporary: Art. 64 ZORZFS sets it for 2024-2028 and the general rate is 19% (FURS); the tax file uses the rate in force.

structure.entity: druzba z omejeno odgovornostjo (d.o.o.), a private limited company holding securities
structure.payout_notes: Dividends paid to a resident individual shareholder bear the 25% final withholding income tax (Art. 132 ZDoh-2; FURS guide of 4 Aug 2026), with no allowance. A buy-back of the shareholder's shares by the company is also taxed as a dividend (LIFO), reduced by the cost of the shares. Loans to shareholders and private use of company assets were not researched.
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: Dividend exclusion: the payer must be subject to Slovenian or a comparable profit tax; dividends from a non-EU company resident in a country with a profit tax below 12.5% on the Ministry of Finance list are not excluded, and dividends paid out of untaxed reserves are not excluded (PwC). 5% of dividends received counts as a non-deductible expense (FURS guide, section 5.1). No minimum holding applies to dividends (PwC). Gains on shares: the 50% exemption needs a stake of at least 8% for 6 months and one employee (FURS), which a passive portfolio company does not meet. Dividends from funds and ETFs (not companies) were not researched. Whether a passive holding company meets the substance tests for treaty benefits was not researched.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: Not researched: tax on liquidation proceeds and on sale of the d.o.o. shares by the family (a gain on shares is capital gain under ZDoh-2, 25% falling to 0% after 15 years).

capital_gains.summary: Gains realised by the d.o.o. on listed shares are part of its taxable profit and bear corporate income tax at 22% (2024-2028). The only relief, a 50% exemption for gains on disposal of a shareholding, needs an interest of at least 8% in capital or management, held for at least 6 months, and at least one employee in that period; a passive holding of listed minority stakes qualifies for none of it. Unrealised gains are not taxed.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: 50% exemption only for stakes of at least 8% held 6 months with one employee; losses on such disposals are then recognised at 50% (FURS guide, section 5.1).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: The 22% rate applies to 2024-2028; the general rate is 19%. Pillar Two top-up tax (ZMD) applies only to large groups and was not examined.

open_questions: Article numbers of ZDDPO-2 (24, 25, 60, 75) come from the FURS guide and PwC; the statute text at PisRS could not be read by the tool.
capital_gains.rate_basis: 22% corporate income tax (FURS: 22% for 2024-2028 under Art. 64 ZORZFS) on the whole gain. Private business sale: the family holding has no employee and the exemption needs an 8% stake, so 22% is used. Real estate gains were not examined for the company (foreign: null).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Not relevant: all income of the company is taxable profit.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: None for the company (the personal 15-year rule does not apply).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide profits of a resident company are taxed.

dividends.summary: Dividends received by the d.o.o. are excluded from its tax base (Art. 24 ZDDPO-2), but 5% of the dividends received is treated as a non-deductible expense, so the effective rate is 5% x 22% = 1.1%. No minimum holding is required. Foreign withholding tax is not credited against the corporate tax, because the dividend is excluded in the gross amount.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: The payer must be subject to Slovenian CIT or a comparable profit tax; dividends from non-EU low-tax (below 12.5%) countries on the Ministry of Finance list and from untaxed reserves are not excluded.

open_questions: Whether foreign dividends from an investment fund or ETF qualify for the exclusion was not researched (only dividends of companies were).

Whether foreign withholding tax can be credited when the dividend is excluded (Art. 75 ZDDPO-2): the FURS clarification 0920-13147/2022-3 treats it as a tax booked outside the profit, so no credit is assumed.
dividends.rate_basis: 22% corporate income tax x 5% of the dividend (non-deductible flat expense) = 1.1% (FURS guide section 5.1 and 4.0). Foreign withholding is lost, not credited.
dividends.withholding_outbound: The d.o.o. withholds the 25% dividend tax when it pays the family (see structure payout terms).
dividends.treaty_network: A Slovenian d.o.o. is a treaty resident (59 treaties per PwC).
dividends.holding_company_notes: This regime is the company itself.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if the individual has a registered permanent residence, a habitual abode, a centre of personal and economic interests in Slovenia, or is present more than 183 days in a tax year (PwC).

routes.name: EU/EEA free movement
routes.requirements: Register residence for stays over 3 months; no investment requirement.

routes.requirements: Permit for a purpose such as employment, business/self-employment or family reunification; no investor-visa route found (not verified).

corporate.summary: CIT is 22% for 2024-2028 (Art. 64 ZORZFS; the general rate is 19%) (FURS). Dividends received are excluded from the base (Art. 24 ZDDPO-2) with 5% treated as a non-deductible expense, with no minimum holding; the payer must be subject to a comparable profit tax, and non-EU payers in countries below 12.5% on the Ministry of Finance list are excluded. Gains on shares are exempt at 50% only for stakes of at least 8% held 6 months with an employee (PwC; FURS guide).

Press headlines in 2026 referred to a ministry proposal on capital gains (30% for 5 years, 0 after 20 years) later abandoned; not verified.
